title: Obadiah Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Obadiah chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Obadiah Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Obadiah Chapter 1.

questions.question: What is the vision of Obadiah concerning?
questions.explanation: The vision of Obadiah is specifically about Edom as stated in Obadiah 1:1.

questions.question: According to Obadiah, how has the Lord made Edom among the heathen?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:2 states that the Lord has made Edom small among the heathen and greatly despised.

questions.question: True or False: The pride of Edom's heart has deceived him.
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:3 confirms that the pride of Edom's heart has deceived him.

questions.question: What analogy does the Lord use to describe Edom's arrogance?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:4 mentions that even if Edom exalts itself as the eagle, the Lord will bring him down.

questions.question: In Obadiah 1:5, what is suggested about thieves and robbers concerning Edom?
options: They would not come at all
They would take more than enough
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that if thieves or robbers came to Edom, they would leave some grapes, emphasizing how Edom is completely cut off.

questions.question: True or False: All men of Edom's confederacy have been loyal and have not deceived him.
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:7 states that the men at peace with Edom have deceived him and prevailed against him.

questions.question: What will happen to the wise men of Edom according to the Lord?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:8 indicates that the Lord will destroy the wise men out of Edom.

questions.question: According to Obadiah 1:10, what will cover Edom due to his violence against Jacob?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:10 states that shame shall cover Edom for his violence against his brother Jacob.

questions.question: True or False: Edom rejoiced in the day of Jacob's destruction.
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:12 states that Edom should not have rejoiced over Judah when they were destroyed.

questions.question: What does Obadiah say Edom should not have done during Jacob's calamity?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:13 specifies that Edom should not have looked on the day of Jacob's calamity.

questions.question: In what order does God promise to bring Edom down?
options: Before the day of the Lord
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:14 mentions that Edom will be judged in the day of distress.

questions.question: What is the ultimate fate of the house of Esau as stated in Obadiah 1:18?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:18 states that the house of Esau will be as stubble and will be devoured.

questions.question: True or False: The day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen.
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:15 confirms that the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen.

questions.question: What will the house of Jacob possess according to Obadiah 1:17?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:17 states that the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.

questions.question: What instruction is given first in Obadiah 1?
options: Let us rise up against Edom
Behold, I have made thee small
The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee
questions.correctAnswer: Let us rise up against Edom
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:1 presents the instruction to arise against Edom first.

medium.title: Obadiah Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Obadiah Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the wise men of Edom according to Obadiah?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:8 states that the LORD will destroy the wise men out of Edom, indicating a complete removal of understanding and wisdom from that place.

questions.question: What is said about the pride of Edom in Obadiah?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:3 mentions that the pride of Edom's heart hath deceived them, leading to their downfall.

questions.question: According to Obadiah 1:10, what shame will cover Edom?
options: Shame for their violence against Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: Shame for their violence against Jacob
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:10 states that Edom will be covered with shame due to their violence against their brother Jacob.

questions.question: Shall the mighty men of Teman be dismayed according to Obadiah?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:9 indicates that the mighty men of Teman shall be dismayed, confirming the impending judgment against Edom.

questions.question: What should Edom not have done on the day of Jacob's calamity?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:12 warns Edom that they should not have rejoiced over the children of Judah during their destruction.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:14 imply about Edom's actions during Jacob's distress?
options: They cut off those who escaped
questions.correctAnswer: They cut off those who escaped
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:14 states that Edom should not have stood in the crossway to cut off those of Jacob's that did escape.

questions.question: According to Obadiah, what will happen to the house of Esau?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:18 declares that there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, indicating complete destruction.

questions.question: Is it true that Edom was warned not to enter the gates during calamity?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:13 clearly indicates that Edom should not have entered the gate of God's people during their calamity.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:15 say about the day of the LORD?
options: It is near upon all the heathen
questions.correctAnswer: It is near upon all the heathen
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:15 states that the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen, emphasizing the coming judgment.

questions.question: What does Obadiah teach about the consequences of pride?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:3-4 illustrates that pride deceives and ultimately leads to downfall, as indicated by God's promise to bring Edom down.

questions.question: According to Obadiah, what will happen to the children of Israel after their captivity?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:20 states that the captivity of the children of Israel will possess the land of the Canaanites, indicating restoration.

questions.question: Edom's actions during Jacob's distress were considered righteous. True or False?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:12-14 shows that Edom's actions were wrong and that they acted pridefully and maliciously against Jacob during his distress.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:17 promise regarding mount Zion?
options: It will be a place of deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a place of deliverance
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:17 states that upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, highlighting God's promise of hope and salvation.

hard.title: Obadiah Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Obadiah Chapter 1.

questions.question: What will happen to Edom according to Obadiah 1:15?
options: They will be rewarded for their actions
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:15 indicates that 'as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head,' signifying destruction as a consequence of their actions.

questions.question: According to Obadiah 1:17, what will be upon mount Zion?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:17 states, 'But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance,' indicating that Zion will be a place of salvation and holiness.

questions.question: Which house will be like a fire, according to Obadiah 1:18?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:18 describes 'the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame,' indicating their strength against Edom.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:19 say about the possessions of the south?
options: They will possess the mount of Esau
questions.correctAnswer: They will possess the mount of Esau
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:19 states, 'And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau,' indicating a reversal of fortunes.

questions.question: According to Obadiah 1:16, how will the heathen drink?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:16 mentions that 'so shall all the heathen drink continually,' indicating ongoing judgment.

questions.question: What literary device is used in the phrase 'the house of Jacob shall be a fire' in Obadiah 1:18?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the house of Jacob shall be a fire' in Obadiah 1:18 uses metaphor to depict strength and destruction.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of divine retribution similar to Obadiah 1:15?
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:7 states, 'For whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap,' similar to the theme of retribution found in Obadiah 1:15.

questions.question: What will happen to the wise men of Edom, according to Obadiah 1:8?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:8 indicates that the LORD will 'destroy the wise men out of Edom,' showing impending judgment.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:14 warn against?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:12 cautions against looking on the day of a brother's calamity and rejoicing, which is condemned.

questions.question: True or False: The house of Esau will remain according to Obadiah 1:18.
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:18 states that there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, indicating total destruction.

questions.question: True or False: The day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen according to Obadiah 1:15.
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:15 clearly states, 'For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen,' affirming this truth.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:20 say about the captivity of the children of Israel?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:20 states that 'the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites,' indicating restoration.

questions.question: Which theme is fulfilled in Obadiah 1:21 regarding the LORD's kingdom?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:21 concludes that 'the kingdom shall be the LORD'S,' emphasizing His sovereignty and fulfillment of the divine kingship theme.

theological.title: Obadiah Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Obadiah Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:2 indicate about Edom's standing among the nations?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:2 states, 'Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised,' indicating that Edom's pride has resulted in its diminishing status.

questions.question: What is the primary sin of Edom according to Obadiah 1:3?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:3 notes, 'The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee,' highlighting pride as the root cause of Edom's downfall.

questions.question: According to Obadiah 1:4, what will happen to those who exalt themselves?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:4 declares, 'Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle... thence will I bring thee down,' emphasizing God's judgment against pride.

questions.question: What fate is pronounced upon Edom's wise men in Obadiah 1:8?
questions.explanation: In Obadiah 1:8, it states, 'Shall I not in that day... destroy the wise men out of Edom,' indicating the totality of God's judgment.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:10 say will cover Edom because of its violence against Jacob?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:10 states, 'For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee,' indicating the consequences of their actions.

questions.question: How does Obadiah 1:11 illustrate Edom's betrayal during Israel's calamity?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:11 explains, 'In the day that thou stoodest on the other side,' depicting Edom's indifference and betrayal of Israel.

questions.question: What warning does Obadiah 1:12 give regarding Edom's attitude towards Judah's destruction?
options: They should not look on the day of their brother
questions.correctAnswer: They should not look on the day of their brother
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:12 states, 'But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother,' indicating the wrongness of their attitude during Judah's suffering.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:15 reveal about the principle of divine retribution?
options: What Edom did to Israel will go unpunished
Edom's actions will return upon their own head
questions.correctAnswer: Edom's actions will return upon their own head
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:15 states, 'as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee,' illustrating the principle of divine retribution.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in Obadiah 1:17 regarding deliverance for Jacob?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:17 reveals, 'But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance,' showcasing God's mercy toward His chosen people, Jacob.

questions.question: What symbolism is used in Obadiah 1:18 to describe the fate of Esau?
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:18 states, 'the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame,' symbolizing destruction for Esau.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:19 indicate about territorial possession?
options: Israel will possess the lands of others
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will possess the lands of others
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:19 notes that 'they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau,' indicating restoration and possession for Israel.

questions.question: What is the role of the 'saviours' mentioned in Obadiah 1:21?
options: To judge the mount of Edom
questions.correctAnswer: To judge the mount of Edom
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:21 states, 'And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau,' indicating their role in executing God's judgment.

questions.question: What overarching theme about God's sovereignty can be drawn from Obadiah Chapter 1?
options: God judges nations based on their treatment of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God judges nations based on their treatment of Israel
questions.explanation: The entire chapter illustrates the principle that God's judgment is aligned with how nations treat His people, particularly Israel, as seen in multiple verses.

questions.question: What does Obadiah 1:6 teach about God's omniscience?
options: God is unaware of hidden things
God searches out the hidden things of Esau
God is ignorant of the nations’ plans
questions.correctAnswer: God searches out the hidden things of Esau
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:6 states, 'How are the things of Esau searched out!' demonstrating God's omniscience and awareness of all actions.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 10 and 14 convey about Edom's actions?
options: Edom will be rewarded for loyalty
Edom will face judgment for violence and betrayal
questions.correctAnswer: Edom will face judgment for violence and betrayal
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 14 highlight that Edom's violence against Jacob and their betrayal during calamity will result in severe judgment from God.
